assessment.nobel_worthiness: A deep, durable political-economy account of how political institutions, state capacity and policy jointly shape economic outcomes.
assessment.attribution: The three named scholars represent closely connected and highly influential theoretical and empirical strands, though the field has many important contributors.
assessment.maturity: The contribution has shaped research and applied policy analysis for decades and is well tested across contexts.
uncertainties: The breadth of the proposed contribution makes the boundary of a three-person award contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their work transformed analysis of technology, trade exposure and the changing distribution of labour-market opportunity.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn and Hanson form a coherent core for task-based change and trade-shock evidence; Katz is also central to the broader inequality literature.
assessment.maturity: The findings have accumulated over a substantial period and remain central to research and public debate.
uncertainties: Separating the respective effects of technology, trade and institutions remains empirically difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This research linked modern tax theory to credible evidence on behavioural responses and the design of progressive taxation.
assessment.attribution: Saez and Slemrod are particularly central to taxable-income elasticity and optimal-taxation work; Chetty made major related methodological and empirical contributions.
assessment.maturity: The framework is mature and has strongly influenced both public-finance research and tax-policy discussion.
uncertainties: A unified prize citation may understate the distinct contributions of other leading tax scholars, including Stantcheva.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale administrative-data research made intergenerational mobility measurable with unusual precision and changed the empirical study of equality of opportunity.
assessment.attribution: Chetty and Hendren are central to the research program, with Friedman an important collaborator on core mobility measurement.
assessment.maturity: The agenda has produced a large body of replicated and extended work, although it is newer than some foundational candidates.
uncertainties: Measurement of mobility does not by itself settle causal explanations or the policies that improve it.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The demonstration and modelling of reciprocity, fairness and inequity aversion substantially revised standard assumptions about economic behaviour.
assessment.attribution: Fehr and Schmidt are especially strongly associated with the canonical inequity-aversion formulation, while Falk is a leading contributor to the experimental evidence.
assessment.maturity: The contribution is long established, extensively tested and influential across labour, organisational and behavioural economics.
uncertainties: The literature contains several competing models and a broad set of experimental contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection supplied a powerful modern account of trade, productivity and the uneven gains from global integration.
assessment.attribution: Melitz is the indispensable originator of the canonical model; Helpman and Redding made major complementary theoretical and empirical contributions.
assessment.maturity: The framework has become a standard workhorse in international trade and has generated extensive empirical evidence.
uncertainties: The appropriate allocation of credit among the wider heterogeneous-firm trade literature is not straightforward.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their work gave rigorous economic content to the long-run valuation of exhaustible resources, natural capital and sustainability.
assessment.attribution: Dasgupta and Heal are clear foundational figures for the stated contribution.
assessment.maturity: The underlying theory is longstanding and increasingly salient for environmental accounting and policy.
uncertainties: Translation from inclusive-wealth concepts to reliable policy metrics remains contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification made economists more explicit about what data can and cannot identify under credible assumptions.
assessment.attribution: Manski is the foundational figure, while Tamer and Molinari made major contributions to moment inequalities and the usable inference toolkit.
assessment.maturity: The approach is mature, technically influential and broadly used where point identification is implausible.
uncertainties: Its methodological importance may be less readily expressible as a single discovery than more unified substantive contributions.
